# Connection map (generated by `python cad/connection_map.py`; provisional)

Every conductor from its pin in the electronics box to its pin at the machine. Pins of the controller come from `board_config.h`; cables, lengths and conductor counts from `cad/wiring.py`. Nothing here is measured or verified.

## Inside the electronics box

| Controller pin | Goes to | Function |
|---|---|---|
| U1.GPIO4 | D_X.STEP | X step |
| U1.GPIO5 | D_Y.STEP | Y step |
| U1.GPIO6 | D_Z.STEP | Z step |
| U1.GPIO7 | D_A.STEP | A step |
| U1.GPIO15 | D_B.STEP | B step |
| U1.GPIO16 | D_P.STEP | P step |
| U1.GPIO17 | D_X.DIR | X direction |
| U1.GPIO18 | D_Y.DIR | Y direction |
| U1.GPIO8 | D_Z.DIR | Z direction |
| U1.GPIO9 | D_A.DIR | A direction |
| U1.GPIO10 | D_B.DIR | B direction |
| U1.GPIO11 | D_P.DIR | P direction |
| U1.GPIO12 | D_X.EN, D_Y.EN, D_Z.EN, D_A.EN, D_B.EN, D_P.EN | drivers enable (low = on) |
| U1.GPIO42 | OPTO1.OUT | motor power OK, after the contactor |
| U1.GPIO13 | T1.DI | head link transmit (reclaims the reserved UART TX) |
| U1.GPIO14 | T1.RO | head link receive (reclaims the reserved UART RX) |

## Power and safety nets

| From | To | What |
|---|---|---|
| PSU24.+ | F1 (fuse) to K1 main contacts 13-14 | 24 V from the supply to the contactor |
| K1.14 | D_X.VM, D_Y.VM, D_Z.VM, D_A.VM, D_B.VM, D_P.VM and the tool rail fuse | 24 V after the contactor: motors and tools |
| K1.14 via divider | OPTO1.IN | motor power OK sense |
| PSU5.+ | U1.5V, D_*.VIO, T1.VCC, ENABLE_5V source | 5 V logic, separate from the motors |
| ENABLE_5V | C8.3 to ES1.21, ES1.22 to AB1.21, AB1.22 to C8.4 (ENABLE_OK), then C7.7 to HB.ENABLE | the enable loop |
| PSU24.+ via ES1.11-12 | K1.A1, K1.A2 to PSU24.- | the e-stop opens the contactor coil |

## Tool connector (12 circuits) on the head board, by tool

Circuits 1-2 switched 24 V, 3-4 ground, 5 logic 5 V, 6 identification (1-wire). Circuits 7-12 by tool:

| Tool | Circuit: signal (kind) |
|---|---|
| injector | 7: plunger motor A+ (phase); 8: plunger motor A- (phase); 9: plunger motor B+ (phase); 10: plunger motor B- (phase) |
| probe | 7: stylus trigger contact (NC to ground) (in); 11: stylus force, optional (analog) |
| scalpel | 7: guard servo (pwm); 8: guard closed sensor (in) |
| drill | 7: motor speed (pwm); 8: motor enable (out); 9: tachometer (in); 11: motor current (analog) |
| fluid | 7: pump 1 (pwm); 8: pump 2 (pwm); 9: line valve (out); 11: line pressure (analog) |
| gripper | 7: jaw motor A+ (phase); 8: jaw motor A- (phase); 9: jaw motor B+ (phase); 10: jaw motor B- (phase); 11: jaw force (analog) |
| cautery | 7: pulse gate (out); 11: tip current (analog) |
| sensor | 7: light source (pwm); 11: detector (analog) |

## Parts that must be fitted

- E-stop and ABORT button with two normally closed contacts each (dual contact): contact 1 for the contactor coil and the ABORT pin, contact 2 for the enable loop
- RS-485 transceivers with automatic direction control at the controller (T1) and at the head board (T2)
- Head board: microcontroller, high-side tool power switch and the discrete AND of the enable loop and the power permit (see wiring.py HEAD_BOARD and HW_CUTOFF_NOTE)
- Four changeover relays or analog switches on the head board that route circuits 7-10 either to the plunger motor phases or to the head outputs, selected from the tool identifier; unpowered, the circuits are disconnected from both
